claims.text: Aromatase inhibitors (anastrozole, exemestane, letrozole) reduce recurrence more than tamoxifen in postmenopausal women
claims.quote: Aromatase inhibitors (anastrozole, exemestane, letrozole) block peripheral conversion of androgens to estrogen in postmenopausal women. These medications have been shown to be more effective than tamoxifen at reducing risk of breast cancer recurrence in postmenopausal women (19).
claims.locator: Endocrine therapy and other therapies for ER-positive breast cancer

claims.text: Premenopausal women with high-risk disease can take an aromatase inhibitor together with ovarian suppression (GnRH agonist or antagonist, or oophorectomy)
claims.quote: Aromatase inhibitors are also considered as therapy for premenopausal women with high-risk disease. These patients also require ovarian suppression, with gonadotropin receptor agonists or antagonists or oophorectomy.
claims.locator: Endocrine therapy and other therapies for ER-positive breast cancer

claims.text: Tamoxifen is also used in postmenopausal women who can't tolerate aromatase inhibitors
claims.quote: Tamoxifen is give to premenopausal women or to postmenopausal women who cannot tolerate aromatase inhibitors.
claims.locator: Endocrine therapy and other therapies for ER-positive breast cancer

claims.text: Fulvestrant: selective estrogen receptor degrader (binds and downregulates the ER); for ER+ metastatic disease, alone or with CDK4/6 inhibitors
claims.quote: Fulvestrant is a selective estrogen receptor degrader (SERD) that competitively binds to and downregulates the estrogen receptor. It is used for treatment of ER-positive, metastatic breast cancer alone or in combination with other therapies, such as CDK4/6 inhibitors (25).
claims.locator: Endocrine therapy and other therapies for ER-positive breast cancer

claims.text: CDK4/6 inhibitors (ribociclib, abemaciclib): HR+, HER2− disease, mainly advanced or metastatic, given with endocrine therapy
claims.quote: Cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) inhibitors (ribociclib, abemaciclib) are targeted therapies used in the treatment of hormone receptor-positive (HR+), HER2-negative breast cancer, particularly in advanced or metastatic disease (26). These agents are typically used in combination with endocrine therapy.
claims.locator: Endocrine therapy and other therapies for ER-positive breast cancer

claims.text: HER2+: trastuzumab is given with chemotherapy, for a year as adjuvant tx or until progression if metastatic; pertuzumab is added if lymph nodes are involved
claims.quote: Women with a HER2-positive breast cancer are treated with anti-HER2 targeted therapy. The monoclonal antibody trastuzumab, in combination with chemotherapy, substantially reduces recurrence and mortality rates. Trastuzumab is continued for a year in the adjuvant setting or until disease progression in the metastatic setting. If lymph nodes are involved, adding pertuzumab to trastuzumab improves disease-free survival.

claims.text: Chemo: combination regimens beat single drugs; dose-dense regimens over 4–6 mo are preferred; a common one is ACT (doxorubicin + cyclophosphamide, then paclitaxel)
claims.quote: Combination chemotherapy regimens are more effective than a single medication. Dose-dense regimens given for 4 to 6 months are preferred; in dose-dense regimens, the time between doses is shorter than that in standard-dose regimens. There are many regimens; a commonly used one is ACT (doxorubicin plus cyclophosphamide followed by paclitaxel).

claims.text: Triple negative: an immune checkpoint inhibitor (eg, pembrolizumab) with chemotherapy
claims.quote: Immunotherapy is typically used to treat triple-negative breast cancer. This includes immune checkpoint inhibitors (eg, pembrolizumab), which is used in combination with chemotherapy (27).
